justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add optional `Location.contact` but retain deprecated `Location.telecom` for flat contact points.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 contacts, but creates overlapping contact representations requiring precedence and conflict rules.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of representing richer grouped contact details is reasonable, and removing the flat field makes `Location.contact` the single canonical contact surface. A less-breaking base design could preserve old instances, but it would duplicate the same fact on the same resource and risk indefinite divergence between `telecom` and `contact.telecom`, so the breakage is probably justified rather than clearly avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would add `Location.contact` and keep `Location.telecom` as deprecated for one or more releases, with rules that flat contact points map to `contact.telecom`. That preserves most R4 data and client paths, but it does not fully solve grouped contact metadata and would require reconciliation when both old and new elements are populated.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain `Location.physicalType` with broadened wording and value set, or keep it as a deprecated alias while adding `Location.form`.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The main cost is living with an outdated element name or temporary alias, which is modest compared with a wire-level rename.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Broadening the concept to include virtual forms is reasonable, but the R6 goal did not require removing the R4 path. Under the calibration rules, retaining a nonoptimal old name plus clearer definitions is a serious backward-compatible option, so the rename looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have kept `physicalType` as the base element and updated its definition and example value set to include non-physical or virtual forms. Alternatively, `form` could have been added while `physicalType` remained as a deprecated alias with a simple equivalence rule. Either design would preserve most R4-valid instances with only moderate naming and cleanup tradeoffs.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the R4 opening-hours backbone and add a separate Availability-based element or deprecated aliases.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 schedule instances only by maintaining duplicate schedule models, reconciliation rules, and implementation burden.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Using a reusable `Availability` datatype is a coherent R6 design goal, especially where multiple resources need comparable schedule and exception modeling. A less-breaking design exists, but it would leave two same-resource schedule representations and make canonical interpretation harder, so the level of breakage is probably justified if the goal was a clean shared model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best alternative would introduce a new optional Availability-valued element, or retain the old `hoursOfOperation` backbone children as deprecated aliases that map into `Availability.availableTime`. This would preserve R4 instances for common opening-hours cases, but it is incomplete for richer R6 availability periods and would create long-term ambiguity when old and new schedule data disagree.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `availabilityExceptions` as a free-text shortcut while adding structured `notAvailableTime` entries.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve old exception text, but leaves two places for closure information and weakens adoption of structured periods.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving exception information into `Availability.notAvailableTime` is a reasonable cleanup because exceptions are part of availability, not a separate Location-level concern. Keeping the R4 string would reduce breakage, but it would duplicate closure semantics and create conflict risk with structured periods, so the breaking consolidation is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `Location.availabilityExceptions` as deprecated text and recommended migration to `hoursOfOperation.notAvailableTime.description`. That covers existing R4 data, but it only handles unstructured exceptions and would require rules for how the deprecated text interacts with multiple R6 `notAvailableTime` entries.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `Location.type` as role/function and add a distinct service-type element for services available at the location.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Adds another classification field, but avoids silent semantic repurposing of an existing path.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of modeling available services is reasonable, but changing the meaning and preferred terminology of the existing `Location.type` path risks semantic breakage for R4 data and consumers. A distinct service-type element would meet the R6 goal while preserving the old role/function semantics with only moderate model-surface cost, so the break appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep R4 `Location.type` for location role or function, retain or deprecate its old terminology, and add an explicit service classification element for the new service-type value set. This would make migration intent visible instead of overloading a familiar path with changed meaning.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed because R4 strings remain JSON-string-compatible with R6 markdown.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Generated primitive wrappers and rendering or sanitization behavior may change, but this is not a base R4-to-R6 instance break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing formatted descriptive text is reasonable, and the wire representation remains a JSON string. Because ordinary R4 `string` values are preserved as R6 `markdown`, this is better calibrated as a low-risk type widening rather than a breaking base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Retaining `string` would avoid some code-generation differences, but it would not communicate markdown rendering semantics to tooling. Under the calibration rules, the backward-compatible-alternative question is not applicable because the change preserves R4 instances rather than requiring a less-breaking replacement design.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional R6 addition; R4 instances are preserved, and R4 extensions are downgrade mitigations rather than base-design alternatives.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 downgrade may need extensions or lose data, but the additive R6 element is not an R4-to-R6 base break.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional virtual-service details is the least disruptive base R6 mechanism for a new capability and does not invalidate R4 Location instances. The reported risk is primarily R6-to-R4 representability, so scoring an R4 extension strategy as a backward-compatible alternative would confuse mitigation with base-design compatibility.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R6 base design is needed for the upgrade direction: absence of `virtualService` in R4 data remains acceptable in R6. Cross-version extensions can preserve this content when downgrading to R4, but they are not a less-breaking alternative to the optional R6 base element.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Optional R6 classification additions; R4-to-R6 compatibility is unaffected.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R4 round-trip may rely on extensions or local mapping, but that is a downgrade concern rather than a less-breaking R6 base alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: First-class coded location and characteristic fields are reasonable optional additions for R6 directories and do not reject existing R4 instances. The compatibility issue is that R6-only content has no R4 core target, which is outside the backward-compatible-alternative judgment for R4-to-R6 base breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Standard extensions can help R4 systems carry these classifications, but that is a cross-version mitigation. Since the R6 fields are optional additions and preserve old instances, there is no applicable less-breaking base R6 design to score.
